newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas rises with cold tempeartures.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas rises with cold tempeartures.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices rose sharply Friday as cold weather drained supplies, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices were up an average of 30 cents to the C$2.60-2.65 per gigajoule (GJ) area, though deals were reported done anywhere from C$2.50 early to a high of C$2.85.
"They revised the weather forecasts. We were supposed to get warmer this weekend, but now they're saying highs will only be -15 (degrees Celsius)," one Calgary-based trader said.
Temperatures in Calgary today were about -22 degrees Celsius.
At Sumas, Wash., the western Canadian export point, prices gained about 20 cents to the low-$3.30s per million British thermal units (mmBtu). Deals were reported done in the $3.10-3.50 range.
Adding support to the market was news that there was a problem at Westcoast Energy's McMahon gas plant in northeast British Columbia.
The company said processing output at the plant would be reduced to 76 percent on Saturday, 82 percent on Sunday and 97 percent on Monday due to rescheduled repairs at the plant.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices rose by about 25 cents to the low-$4 per mmBtu area as cold weather was forecast for the area through early next week.
